steps.title: Show the current time on the home page as an ISO 8601 string
steps.intent: On the home page, determine the current time and render it as a human-readable ISO 8601 date-time string in the operator's local timezone, current as of the moment the page is rendered.
steps.acceptance: On page render the home page captures the current time once and renders it as a non-empty ISO 8601 date-time string in the operator's local timezone whose value matches the operator's browser current time within 3 seconds, evaluated only at render time; the displayed timestamp is not required to tick or update live. It is never a UNIX epoch or other non-ISO format and never in the future. If the clock is unavailable or yields no value or an invalid value, the page shows a generic error message (e.g. "Error processing request") rather than an empty string, a refusal, or a setup hint.
steps.stand_in: ISO 8601 local-time representation with UTC offset at second precision, e.g. "2026-08-23T16:50:09+01:00" (no milliseconds), confirmed by the operator's answer to q-iso-format; local timezone resolved from the browser per runbooks/domain-expert/common.md ("Timestamps display in the operator's local timezone") and issue #40. Per the operator's answer to q-refresh, the timestamp is captured once at render and the 3-second window is evaluated only at render time (no live ticking).

verification_targets.check: The rendered time string is non-empty.
The rendered string parses as a valid ISO 8601 date-time and is not a UNIX epoch integer or other non-ISO format.
The parsed rendered time equals the operator's browser current time within a 3-second tolerance at render time and is not in the future.

boundary_cases.description: If the time source yields no value, the view must not render an empty string; it shows a generic error message (e.g. "Error processing request") instead, not a refusal or a setup hint.
If the system/browser clock is unavailable or returns an invalid or future value, the view shows a generic error message rather than a refusal, a hint, an invalid value, or a UNIX epoch.
At the day boundary the ISO date portion rolls over correctly (23:59:59 advances to the next day 00:00:00) in the local timezone.
